sentences.text: Paraprevotella was proposed as a new genus of the family 'Prevotellaceae' for two anaerobic, Gram-negative rods isolated from human faeces.
A study reported that Paraprevotella strains isolated from the faecal microbiome of healthy human donors are potent trypsin-degrading commensals.
That study reported that they recruit trypsin to the bacterial surface through type IX secretion system-dependent polysaccharide-anchoring proteins, promoting trypsin autolysis.
The same report describes Paraprevotella colonisation protecting IgA from trypsin degradation and inhibiting lethal infection with a mouse coronavirus that depends on trypsin-like proteases.
A genomic comparison of peptidases across 44 Prevotella and two Paraprevotella species found metallopeptidases to be the most predominant catalytic type.
